The same dead pattern exists in updateEvent. This is a verifiable logic defect introduced by the diff: cancellation paths where the reference lacks externalCalendarId would call delete/update with an undefined calendarId, failing to delete remote events.

judged_text: deleteEvent copies the same broken pattern: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares against undefined and can never match a real calendar. Cancellation of a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId passes calendarId=undefined to calendar.events.delete, so the remote calendar event is never deleted and orphaned events accumulate in users' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar id like `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the `find` runs), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined/null`, so it will not match a real calendar externalId and returns `undefined`. This makes the selected/calendarId resolution incorrect for references lacking `externalCalendarId` (it won’t select a destination calendar), which can lead to updating/deleting against the wrong calendar or failing to delete the intended remote event.
